water_surface.packing: same [height_min_m, height_max_m] as the height atlas, mapped to [0,65534]
water_surface.runtime: surface = (code==65535) ? NO_WATER : height_min_m + code/65534*(height_max_m-height_min_m); depth = max(0, surface - terrain_height). Unifies lakes and rivers; no rim scan, no rain-fill, valid across terrain edits.
water_surface.lake_surface: authoritative NVE hoyde, or a level read off the LiDAR water surface inside the polygon (metres above sea level)
water_surface.river_surface: the UNCARVED leaf-DTM ground height under the channel — the river surface sits ON the terrain, and the water column comes from the trench carved beneath it (see river_carve_depth_by_order_m); raised to the lake surface, never lowered to it, where a river meets a lake.

sources.rivers: https://kart.nve.no/enterprise/rest/services/Elvenett1/MapServer (layer 2 elvenett — the authoritative network, serialised as polylines)
sources.rivers_order_overlay: https://kart.nve.no/enterprise/rest/services/Elvenett1/MapServer (layer 1 hovedelv — rasterised for the stream-order upgrade only, not serialised)

identity_fields.note: objectid is Esri-internal and NOT persisted — it is not stable across NVE service updates.

width_model.note: centerline buffered to this FULL width (m) by stream order, then scaled; drives pixel coverage only.

lake_levels.method: a published NVE hoyde is used verbatim. For a lake without one: the mean of the 1-25th percentile band of the void-repaired DTM inside the polygon (LiDAR returns the water surface), ignoring island pixels, minus margin_m, then capped at the 25th percentile of the land ring just outside the polygon so the estimate cannot stand above the terrain around it.

lake_bathymetry.ramp_profile_m: a STRAIGHT ramp: depth = carve_depth_m * clip((metres from the waterline) / shore_ramp_m, 0, 1), flat from there inward. shore_ramp_m = carve_depth_m / shore_slope_m_per_m, so at slope 1.0 a 20 m bed takes 20 m of shore. A body too small to reach carve_depth_m has its profile scaled up just far enough to reach min_depth_m at its deepest sample
lake_bathymetry.islands: lake polygon holes are rasterised as lake so the surface runs through them, but their DTM height is left alone and they act as shore for the ramp; depth = max(0, level - terrain) hides them
lake_bathymetry.rationale: LiDAR returns the lake SURFACE as terrain height, so without a carve the water plane and the terrain are coincident. Safe for the solver: ramped, never breaks the rim, and the lake level is authored and pinned.

river_bathymetry.level: the ground under the channel's own centreline, spread flat across the samples that centreline seeded — so the water surface is level ACROSS a channel and descends ALONG it
river_bathymetry.profile: depth = depth_by_order(order) * smoothstep(distance from bank / modelled channel half-width), cut in full while the sample is within bank_tolerance_m of the water level and tapering to nothing at twice that; a one-sample channel takes full depth as a step
river_bathymetry.rationale: the river water surface is the uncarved ground under the channel, so the trench is the entire water column. Carving down rather than raising the surface keeps a river in its landscape instead of on top of it; levelling across the channel and stopping the carve at the waterline keeps it off the cliffs beside it.

water_id.runtime: isLake = v >= 16; isRiver = v == 1; isOcean = v == 2; lake_id = v - 16 keys into lakes.json for the authored level. Tile byte offsets are identical to the height atlas.
water_id.downsample: categorical; precedence lake > river > ocean > dry, majority lake id; never averaged

rivers.note: z is the sampled DTM BED — the floor of the carved channel — burn against this. level is the water SURFACE (the ground above that channel, or the lake's authored level inside a lake span) — pin to this. Loaded once, resident; not streamed.

validation.clip_note: vertices outside the export region are dropped and a feature that re-enters is split; sampling them would clamp to an edge pixel and fabricate bed, level and lake id.
validation.descent_note: reported only; not corrected. The runtime burn's running-minimum enforces descent.
validation.flowdir_note: source vertex order is authoritative; Z is an independent QA signal only and never flips a segment.
validation.connectivity_note: orphans are segments with neither an upstream nor a downstream neighbour; a few at the region border are expected, many in the interior are not.
